{{Quote|&hellip;a primitive code involving two alternating symbols. Specific combinations of these symbols stand in for letters -- just as binary notation provides a symbolic representation of words and numbers.|Kyle Katarn explaining the code to Jan Ors|<ref name="JK" />}}
A '''communications code''' that utilized combinations of two symbols to represents letters of a language. The symbols could have the form of clicks, either in rapid succession, or silence between them. It was considered obsolete by the time of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and few remembered it during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="JK">''[[Dark Forces: Jedi Knight]]''</ref><ref name="JKaudio">[[Dark Forces: Jedi Knight (audio drama)|''Dark Forces: Jedi Knight'' audio drama]]</ref>

==History==
This communications code was considered "primitive" by the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]],<ref name="JK" /> suggesting that it had been used during the time of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]]. The concept of using combination of binary symbols to represent letters made this code comparable to the also ancient and obsolete [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] code [[dadita]].

During the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]], when most [[droid/Legends|droids]] could understand voice commands, and more advanced codes were the norm, it became obsolete; it was not even taught in the [[Carida Academy/Legends|Academy of Carida]]. One of the few individuals who still remembered the code was [[farmer/Legends|farmer]] [[Morgan Katarn]], who found it a practical way to send signals to his simplistic [[Agrirobot/Legends|agricultural droids]]. He also taught it to his son [[Kyle Katarn|Kyle]].<ref name="JKaudio" /> 

When Katarn led some [[Sulon]]ese dissidents to [[Ruusan/Legends|Ruusan]], far from the Empire, he taught the code to them so that they could use it to safely communicate between themselves and employ as a sort of friend-or-foe identification system.<ref name="JKaudio" /> Years later, in [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], the planet was attacked by the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]] and the [[Vengeance Battle Group]]; the survivors of the [[Battle of Fort Nowhere]] retreated to [[Unidentified Ruusan temple|the ruins of a Jedi temple]] and [[Grif Grawley]] [[transmitter/Legends|transmitted]] a message in loop pointing to fifty-six [[kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] south of Fort Nowhere, possibly in an attempt to attract more survivors.<ref name="JK" /><ref name="JKaudio" />

Soon after, Katarn's son with [[Jan Ors]] in the ''[[Moldy Crow/Legends|Moldy Crow]]'' [[mission to Ruusan|arrived on the planet in order to stop Jerec]]. Scanning the comm channels, Kyle noticed the regular repetition pattern of the clicks<ref name="JK" /> and recognised it as the code used by his father.<ref name="JKaudio" /> With help from the ship's computer,<ref name="JK" /> they translated the message and met with the survivors.

==Behind the scenes==
The novella ''[[Dark Forces: Jedi Knight]]'' mentions a primitive code of alternative binary symbols, whose combinations form letters whose description matches the real-life [[Wikipedia:Morse code|Morse code]]. In the novella it is the ship's computer that translates it. In the [[Dark Forces: Jedi Knight (audio drama)|audio adaptation]] it is mentioned that [[Morgan Katarn]] knew it and utilized it with his old droids, taught it to his son [[Kyle Katarn]], and later to [[Sulon/Legends|Sulonese]] colonists.
